failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES recovers above -10% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility collapsed to -47.0% at t-1w, indicating severe public transport avoidance. This behavioral shift persists, reducing foot traffic to retail destinations accessible primarily by transit, driving RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -45% in any week
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -30% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite sustained TRANSIT depression below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility swung from -29.3% (t-3w) to +6.0% (t-1w) then back to -32.1% (t-0w), indicating volatile outdoor recreation demand. This volatility reflects uncertainty about activity resumption. When PARKS and RETAIL_REC both decline sharply (as at t-0w), it signals coordinated suppression of discretionary mobility, perpetuating RETAIL_REC decline.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and RETAIL_REC both negative and declining week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS recovers to positive territory while RETAIL_REC remains negative, or RETAIL_REC rises despite PARKS remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM volatility (ranging -10.1% to +2.4%) reflects essential-goods shopping patterns decoupled from discretionary retail. When GROCERY_PHARM is negative or flat, consumers are minimizing all shopping trips, including retail. This suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5% in current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM decline below -5%, or GROCERY_PHARM recovers above +5% without corresponding RETAIL_REC recovery.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below their respective thresholds, or either series recovers above threshold within one week.
